title: Only 7% Can Name These Vintage Items
summary: Cassette tapes, rotary phones and forgotten everyday objects make one fast trip through the past.

landing.intro: Think you know the objects that shaped everyday life before everything went digital? Name ten nostalgic items and see whether you are a true vintage expert.

startPrompt.title: Time Capsule Ready! 📻
startPrompt.copy: Watch a short ad to start the quiz.

about.body:
This quick worldwide-English picture quiz opens a ten-item time capsule filled with once-familiar technology, classroom equipment, kitchen tools and household communication devices. Every question asks you to identify the object shown rather than recall an obscure date or brand.

The selection moves from widely recognised media formats to a few items that may challenge younger players. The photographs are used with permission, and each answer review explains what the object did and why people once relied on it.

Your final percentage reflects only this entertainment challenge. It is a playful measure of vintage-object recognition, not an estimate of your age, memory or knowledge of any particular country or decade.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Study each photograph and choose the one name that best identifies the item shown.
Correctness stays hidden while you play, so trust the visual details and avoid overthinking familiar shapes.
Finish all ten items to reveal your Vintage Score and a complete answer-and-explanation review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz does not determine your age or provide a formal historical assessment.

profiles.title: The Time-Capsule Master
profiles.copy: You recognised the defining details of almost every object, from magnetic media to mechanical office equipment. Very little in this time capsule could catch you out.

profiles.title: The Vintage Expert
profiles.copy: You knew the everyday technology of earlier decades remarkably well. A single unfamiliar silhouette may have kept the collection interesting.

profiles.title: The Nostalgia Natural
profiles.copy: You identified a strong majority of the collection and read the visual clues confidently. Your result suggests an excellent feel for objects from the pre-digital world.

profiles.title: The Retro Spotter
profiles.copy: You recognised many familiar classics while a few specialist items stayed hidden in the past. The review will reveal the small details behind each answer.

profiles.title: The Curious Collector
profiles.copy: Half of the time capsule felt familiar, and half delivered a genuine surprise. That is a strong starting point for a fast visual history challenge.

profiles.title: The Digital-Era Explorer
profiles.copy: Some of these objects belonged to a very different everyday world. You still uncovered useful visual clues, and the review turns every miss into a quick piece of retro knowledge.

insights.overview: Your vintage score at a glance

details.analysisTitle: How to read your Vintage Score
details.analysisCopy: This ten-picture result combines music formats, household tools, classroom objects, office machines and communication technology. Each answer moves the percentage by ten points, while the category breakdown shows where recognition was strongest.
details.roadmapIntro: The headline score is only the first stop. Continue through the report to see which corner of the time capsule felt most familiar.
details.positionCopy: The challenge target is eight correct answers out of ten. Your marker shows how close this attempt came to that entertainment-only benchmark.
details.measuredIntro: The questions span three broad types of once-common objects.

measuredAreas.title: Music and media
measuredAreas.copy: Recognising the formats and portable devices people used before streaming and compact digital storage.

measuredAreas.title: Home and school
measuredAreas.copy: Identifying practical objects that once appeared in kitchens and classrooms.

measuredAreas.title: Office and communication
measuredAreas.copy: Spotting the machines people used to write, copy, save information and stay in touch.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to spot a vintage object
details.tipsIntro: Use these visual clues if you try the time capsule again.

tips.title: Look for moving parts
tips.copy: Dials, cranks, rollers and exposed controls often reveal what a mechanical object was designed to do.

tips.title: Notice the storage medium
tips.copy: Tape, film and magnetic disks have distinctive shapes that separate them from later digital formats.

tips.title: Read the object’s scale
tips.copy: Compare handheld devices with desktop machines and fixed equipment before choosing between similar names.

questions.question: Let's kick things off with a classic: can you name this vintage music keeper?

image.alt: A compact rectangular object containing two visible tape reels

questions.explanation: Cassette tapes stored sound on magnetic tape wound between two small reels and became a defining format for music and home recording.

questions.question: Take a look at this chunky black brick—can you guess what it is?

image.alt: A large black rectangular plastic video cassette

questions.explanation: VHS cassettes carried magnetic videotape and were widely used for home films and recorded television before DVDs became common.

questions.question: Can you spot the legendary device that let music lovers take their favourite tunes on the go?

image.alt: A portable cassette player with wired headphones

questions.explanation: This is a portable cassette player, commonly known by Sony's famous Walkman name, which made private music listening possible on the move.

questions.question: Before classrooms went digital, this dusty surface was where lessons appeared daily. What is it?

image.alt: A dark classroom writing board covered with chalk marks

questions.explanation: Teachers wrote on chalkboards with sticks of chalk, then erased the dusty marks before beginning the next lesson.

questions.question: What is this hand-cranked kitchen device used to make?

image.alt: A metal hand-cranked roller machine mounted on a kitchen work surface

questions.explanation: A manual pasta maker rolls dough into thin sheets and can cut it into even ribbons such as tagliatelle.

questions.question: This noisy machine once churned out quick copies. Do you recognise it?

image.alt: A large vintage hand-operated office duplicating machine

questions.explanation: A mimeograph used a stencil and ink to duplicate pages before modern photocopiers took over offices and classrooms.

questions.question: What kind of classic communication device is shown here?

image.alt: A tabletop telephone with a circular finger dial

questions.explanation: A rotary phone required the caller to turn the numbered dial once for every digit in the telephone number.

questions.question: This thin plastic square held a tiny amount of computer data. Can you name it?

image.alt: A square flexible magnetic computer storage disk

questions.explanation: Floppy disks stored computer files on a magnetic disk and were widely used before optical discs and flash storage.

questions.question: Which click-clacking mechanical writing device is shown here?

image.alt: A mechanical writing machine with rows of raised keys and a paper carriage

questions.explanation: A mechanical typewriter pressed inked type against paper and produced its familiar clacking sound with every key.

questions.question: A numeric beep from this belt-worn gadget meant finding a telephone. What was it called?

image.alt: A small rectangular electronic device with a numeric screen and belt clip

questions.explanation: A pager received a short alert or telephone number, prompting its wearer to find a phone and return the call.
